landmarks.name: Banc d'Arguin National Park
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its rich biodiversity, especially migratory birds and marine life.

wiki.extract: The Banc d'Arguin National Park of Bay of Arguin lies in Western Africa on the west coast of Mauritania between Nouakchott and Nouadhibou and is the former mouth of the Tamanrasset River. The World Heritage Site is a major site for migratory birds and breeding birds, including flamingos, pelicans and terns. Much of the breeding is on sand banks including the islands of Tidra, Niroumi, Nair, Kijji and Arguim. The surrounding waters are some of the richest fishing waters in western Africa and serve as nesting grounds for the entire western region.

landmarks.name: Chinguetti Mosque
landmarks.writeup: An ancient mosque and one of the oldest in continuous use in the Muslim world, located in the historic town of Chinguetti.

wiki.extract: The Chinguetti Mosque, also known as the Chinguetti Great Mosque, is a Sunni Islam mosque in Chinguetti, Adrar Region, Mauritania. The minaret of this ancient structure is claimed to be the second oldest in continuous use anywhere in the Muslim world.

landmarks.name: Nouakchott
landmarks.writeup: The capital city, serving as the political and economic center of Mauritania.

wiki.extract: Nouakchott is the capital and largest city of Mauritania. Located in the southwestern part of the country, it is one of the largest cities in the Sahara. The city also serves as the administrative and economic center of Mauritania.

landmarks.name: Terjit Oasis
landmarks.writeup: A natural oasis in the Adrar region, popular for its palm groves and natural springs.

wiki.extract: Terjit is an oasis, 45km by road south of Atar and popular with tourists in Mauritania. It nestles in a gorge on the western edge of the Adrar plateau with the palm grove stretching a few hundred meters alongside a stream which emerges from a spring. Terjit is part of the commune of Maaden in the Aoujeft Department.

landmarks.name: Adrar Plateau
landmarks.writeup: A mountainous region with desert landscapes, ancient rock art, and historic caravan routes.

wiki.extract: The Adrar is a highland natural and historical region of the Sahara Desert in northern Mauritania. The Adrar Region, an administrative division of Mauritania, is named after the traditional region. It is sometimes called Adrar Tamar to distinguish it from other areas called Adrar in the Sahara.

cultural_events.name: Maouloud
cultural_events.writeup: A religious festival celebrating the birth of the Prophet Muhammad with prayers, music, and communal gatherings.

wiki.extract: Mouloud is a town located in the southern Dikhil region of Djibouti. It is located around 102 kilometers south of the capital, Djibouti City.

cultural_events.name: Date Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event celebrating the date harvest with markets, cultural performances, and traditional food.

wiki.extract: Al Qassim Date Festival is the largest date festival in the world held annually in the central Al Qassim region of Saudi Arabia. It is estimated that about 300,000 tonnes of dates are sold annually. The festival is also accompanied by heritage activities that attract visitors from neighboring countries. Saudi Arabia has the highest number of palm trees in the world representing around 25% of the world's date production. Al Qassim region, where the festival is held, has more than 8 million palm trees.

food_writeup: Mauritanian cuisine blends Arab, Berber, and African influences, featuring dishes like thieboudienne (fish and rice), camel meat, and rich use of spices and dates.
brief_history: Mauritania gained independence from France in 1960. Historically a crossroads of Saharan trade routes, it has a diverse cultural heritage influenced by Arab-Berber and sub-Saharan African peoples. The country has experienced political instability and efforts toward economic development.
current_conflicts: Mauritania faces challenges related to desertification, economic development, and occasional tensions related to ethnic and social inequalities. There are no active large-scale armed conflicts.
